title: NOAA's El Niño threshold is 0.5°C in the Niño-3.4 region
summary: NOAA's archived ENSO page says El Niño requires a Niño-3.4 sea-surface anomaly of at least +0.5°C, persisting for five overlapping seasons, plus an atmospheric change.
body: NOAA Climate.gov's ENSO page states El Niño criteria as three conditions together. Average sea-surface temperatures in the Niño-3.4 region, 5 degrees north to 5 degrees south and 120 degrees west to 170 degrees west, were at least 0.5 degrees Celsius warmer than average in the preceding month. An anomaly of that size has persisted, or is expected to persist, for five consecutive overlapping three-month periods. And the atmosphere over the tropical Pacific shows one or more of the changes the page associates with El Niño, including weaker than usual easterly trade winds. A warm month by itself is not the criterion the page prints.
